meaning: The mod folder has no config.cpp, so there is nothing for the engine to load.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> to add config.cpp, or mark the folder as a payload bundle by putting its prebuilt PBOs in workspace/<ModName>/Addons/.

meaning: config.cpp has a syntax error, so CfgConvert stops and the PBO never builds.
fix: Open config.cpp at the line given and fix the brace, ';' or array syntax the message names.

meaning: config.cpp declares no CfgPatches class, so the engine does not load the mod's config.
fix: Add class CfgPatches { class <ModName> { units[] = {}; weapons[] = {}; requiredVersion = 0.1; requiredAddons[] = {"DZ_Data"}; }; }; to workspace/<ModName>/config.cpp.

meaning: class CfgPatches is there but declares no patch class, so the mod registers nothing.
fix: Add class <ModName> { units[] = {}; weapons[] = {}; requiredVersion = 0.1; requiredAddons[] = {"DZ_Data"}; }; inside CfgPatches.

meaning: A CfgPatches class writes units, weapons or requiredAddons without [], so the value is not an array.
fix: Write it as an array: units[] = {...}; weapons[] = {...}; requiredAddons[] = {...}; as vanilla does (P:\scripts\config.cpp, class DZ_Scripts).
source: vanilla P:\scripts\config.cpp CfgPatches; dayz-new-mod config.cpp template

meaning: A CfgPatches class has no units[] or weapons[]. A warning only: the mod still loads (vanilla DZ_data_aiconfigs has neither).
fix: Add the missing array, for example units[] = {}; weapons[] = {};, as the dayz-new-mod template does.
source: vanilla P:\DZ\data\aiconfigs\config.cpp (class DZ_data_aiconfigs, empty body); dayz-new-mod config.cpp template

meaning: A CfgPatches class has no requiredAddons[], so its config can load before the vanilla classes it changes.
fix: Add requiredAddons[] = {"DZ_Data"}; plus any other patch classes the mod builds on, as the dayz-new-mod template does.

meaning: A requiredAddons entry is not a CfgPatches class the engine can find: a path, a .pbo or @mod name, the mod's own patch, or a misspelled vanilla DZ_ name.
fix: Use the CfgPatches class name of the addon this mod needs, spelled as in its config.cpp (vanilla ones are under P:\DZ\, for example DZ_Data or DZ_Gear_Camping).
source: Tier 2 conventions/config.md; vanilla CfgPatches under P:\DZ

meaning: The same requiredAddons entry is listed twice.
fix: Remove the second copy from requiredAddons.

meaning: The mod folder has no $PBOPREFIX$, so the PBO has no root for its <ModName>\ paths.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> to add $PBOPREFIX$ with the single line <ModName>.

meaning: $PBOPREFIX$ is not plain ASCII or UTF-8 text (often UTF-16, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes for `echo <ModName> > $PBOPREFIX$`), so its prefix cannot be read.
fix: Save workspace/<ModName>/$PBOPREFIX$ as plain ASCII or UTF-8 holding only the single line <ModName>, for example in PowerShell: Set-Content -Encoding ascii -Path '$PBOPREFIX$' -Value <ModName>.

meaning: $PBOPREFIX$ does not hold exactly the mod name, so the PBO's paths would not resolve.
fix: Set workspace/<ModName>/$PBOPREFIX$ to the single line <ModName> and make config.cpp paths start at <ModName>\.

meaning: The P:\<ModName>\ link is missing, is a real folder, or points away from workspace/<ModName>/, so AddonBuilder cannot read the source.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> --piece junction.

meaning: P:\ is not mounted, so the P:\<ModName>\ link and the vanilla requiredAddons names could not be checked.
fix: Mount P: with /dayz-workdrive, then lint again.

meaning: A CfgMods script module lists a folder that is outside the mod or does not exist, so that module fails to compile.
fix: Point files[] at <ModName>/scripts/<layer> and make sure that folder exists under workspace/<ModName>/.
source: Tier 2 conventions/scripts.md (folder modules); vanilla P:\DZ\data_sakhal\config.cpp CfgMods

meaning: A script module lists the folder of another layer (for example worldScriptModule pointing at 3_Game), so classes compile in the wrong module.
fix: List 3_Game under gameScriptModule, 4_World under worldScriptModule and 5_Mission under missionScriptModule.

meaning: A scripts/ folder holds .c files that no CfgMods script module lists. A warning only: the mod still loads, but the engine ignores those files.
fix: Add the folder to the matching module's files[] in CfgMods > <ModName> > defs, as /dayz-new-mod writes it.
source: Tier 2 conventions/scripts.md (folder modules); dayz-new-mod config.cpp template

meaning: A modded class with an extends clause compiles but is a silent no-op, so the override never runs.
fix: Drop the extends clause: modded class Foo { ... }.

meaning: A file under scripts/ is not a .c file, so it is never compiled.
fix: Rename it to .c if it is script code, or move it out of scripts/.

meaning: A config path points at a .p3d inside the mod that does not exist.
fix: Fix the path in config.cpp or add the .p3d under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\).

meaning: A config or .rvmat path points at a texture or material inside the mod that does not exist.
fix: Fix the path, or add the file under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\); pack images with /dayz-pack-texture.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (missing textures); Tier 2 conventions/assets.md

meaning: A config path points at a file inside the mod that does not exist.
fix: Fix the path in config.cpp or add the file under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\).

meaning: A config or .rvmat path is a disk path (P:\..., workspace\...), which does not exist inside the PBO.
fix: Write the path from the PBO prefix: <ModName>\data\file.paa.

meaning: A config or .rvmat path names a .png, .tga, .jpg or .dds image; the game loads textures as .paa.
fix: Pack the image with /dayz-pack-texture and point the path at the .paa.

meaning: A texture has no role suffix such as _co, _nohq or _smdi, so ImageToPAA cannot pick its format.
fix: Rename the texture with its role suffix (full list in Tier 2 conventions/assets.md) and update the path.

meaning: A .rvmat material cannot be read (an unclosed string or comment), so it fails to load.
fix: Open the .rvmat at the line given and close the string or comment.

pattern: 0x00020005|does not support the client's current filePatching setting
meaning: The server refused the -filePatching client because its serverDZ.cfg has no active allowFilePatching = 1; line.
fix: Re-run /dayz-add-server <instance>; it sets allowFilePatching = 1; in .server/<instance>/serverDZ.cfg.

pattern: Mission script has no main function
meaning: The server loaded an empty or broken mission folder, so players can never spawn.
fix: Check that .server/<instance>/mission/init.c defines main(); re-copy it with /dayz-add-server <instance> --refresh-mission.

meaning: A script error earlier in the same log stopped this script module from compiling; nothing in it runs.
fix: Fix the first SCRIPT (E) line with an @"file,line" location above this one; this line is fallout from it.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (script compile errors); dayz-mod-debugger (first error, not the loudest)

meaning: The script names a class the compiler cannot see: a typo, a class from a higher scripts layer (3_Game cannot see 4_World or 5_Mission), or a class from another mod whose CfgPatches is not in requiredAddons.
fix: Check the spelling and the scripts/ layer of the file named on the line. If the class comes from another mod, add that mod's CfgPatches class to requiredAddons and pass the mod to the gate with --deps.
source: dayz-mod-debugger usual causes (Can't find or missing class errors)

meaning: The script refers to a class, variable or function that is not declared where the compiler looks: a typo, a missing declaration, or a missing CfgPatches requiredAddons entry.
fix: Open the file and line named on the error, fix the name or declare it; if it lives in another mod, add that mod to requiredAddons and to --deps.
source: dayz-mod-debugger usual causes (Can't find or missing class errors)

meaning: The script calls a method that does not exist on that class (a typo, or a vanilla API that changed).
fix: Grep P:\scripts\ for the class named on the line and call a method it really has.
source: dayz-lead example (a method that doesn't exist on ItemBase); Tier 2 Vanilla source search

meaning: Script code used an object reference that was null at run time.
fix: Open the first mod file in the stack trace (points_to) and null-check the object before using it (enscript-style.md, null checks).

meaning: A config or material points at a .paa that is not in the loaded data.
fix: Check the path in config.cpp hiddenSelectionsTextures or the .rvmat against the file under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\), and that the .paa exists with a role suffix such as _co.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (missing textures); Tier 2 conventions/assets.md

meaning: A config model= path points at a .p3d that is not in the loaded data.
fix: Check the model= path in config.cpp against the .p3d under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\).

meaning: A config lookup failed: the class or property is missing from the loaded config, often a misspelled class or a parent that loads after the mod because CfgPatches requiredAddons does not list it.
fix: Find the class path on the line in workspace/<ModName>/config.cpp; fix the name, add the missing property, or add the parent's CfgPatches class to requiredAddons.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (missing config classes); dayz-mod-debugger usual causes

meaning: A modded class with an extends clause compiles but is a silent no-op, so the override never runs.
fix: Drop the extends clause: modded class Foo { ... }.

meaning: config.cpp declares no CfgPatches class, so the engine does not load the mod's config.
fix: Add class CfgPatches { class <ModName> { units[] = {}; weapons[] = {}; requiredVersion = 0.1; requiredAddons[] = {}; }; }; to workspace/<ModName>/config.cpp.

meaning: The DayZ Tools work drive is not mounted, so nothing can build or launch.
fix: Mount P: from DayZ Tools (Tools menu, Mount P drive), then gate again.

meaning: AddonBuilder cannot be found.
fix: Install DayZ Tools from Steam, or set DAYZ_TOOLS_PATH to its install root.

pattern: P:\\Mods\\? (?:does not exist|is a regular folder|junction is dangling)
meaning: P:\Mods\ is not a junction to the DayZ !Workshop folder, so built PBOs would not land where the engine loads them.
fix: Recreate the junction: cmd /c mklink /J P:\Mods "<DayZ install>\!Workshop" (remove a regular P:\Mods folder first).

meaning: P:\Mods\@<ModName>\ exists but was not created by this pipeline; it could be a subscribed or hand-placed mod.
fix: If the folder is yours, remove it (cmd /c rmdir /s /q P:\Mods\@<ModName>) and gate again; otherwise rename the mod.

pattern: P:\\\w+ junction is missing|exists as a real folder, not a link
meaning: The P:\<ModName>\ link to workspace/<ModName>/ is missing or wrong, so AddonBuilder cannot read the source.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> --piece junction.

meaning: $PBOPREFIX$ does not hold exactly the mod name, so the PBO's paths would not resolve.
fix: Set workspace/<ModName>/$PBOPREFIX$ to the single line <ModName> and make config.cpp paths start at <ModName>\.

meaning: The mod folder lacks config.cpp or $PBOPREFIX$, which the build needs.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> to add the missing file.

meaning: /dayz-launch-test found no PBO for a mod on the launch line.
fix: For the mod under test run /dayz-gate build <ModName>; for a dependency, put its @mod under P:\Mods\ first.
source: docs/dayz-modding.md Troubleshooting (Mod has no built PBO)

meaning: The server instance has no serverDZ.cfg, mission folder or template junction.
fix: Run /dayz-add-server <instance>.

meaning: The DayZ Diag binary that both server and client need is missing.
fix: Verify the DayZ install in Steam, or set DAYZ_DIAG_PATH to DayZDiag_x64.exe.

meaning: Something still holds the server port after the gate stopped DayZDiag.
fix: Close the program holding the port, or run the gate with another --port.

meaning: A bundle PBO ships without its signature; clients that verify signatures reject it.
fix: Put the PBO's .bisign (from the mod's author) next to it in workspace/<ModName>/Addons/ and gate again.

meaning: A capture of the DayZ window looks different from its baseline by more than the shot's threshold.
fix: Open the diff image (red pixels changed). If the change is intended, run gate.py visual <ModName> --accept --shot <id>; if not, send the capture and the diff to the specialist who owns that part of the screen.

meaning: A shot has no baseline yet, so there is no expected look to compare with.
fix: Look at the capture. If it shows the expected look, run gate.py visual <ModName> --accept --shot <id> and gate again.

meaning: A shot was not captured: the client window was hidden or minimized, or the session ended first.
fix: Keep the DayZ client window visible and not minimized during the gate, check the in-game failures in the same report, then gate again.
